say.en: Connect a resistor, a coil and a capacitor in turn to the same AC supply. The current changes in size and also shifts in time. Why? In this lesson: State the phase relation between V and I in R, L and C.

body.en: In a *pure resistor* the current is in phase with the voltage: $i = (V_m/R) \sin ωt$. Ohm's law holds with RMS values, $I = V/R$, and the average power is $P = V_{rms} I_{rms}$. Resistance does not depend on frequency.
body.kn: ಶುದ್ಧ ರೋಧಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಭವಾಂತರ ಒಂದೇ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತವೆ. RMS ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳಿಗೆ I = V/R. ರೋಧ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title.en: On the board: R, L and C with AC

say.en: Let us compare the voltage and current phasors in a pure resistor, a pure inductor and a pure capacitor.
In an inductor the current lags the voltage by 90 degrees. Its opposition is XL equal to 2 pi f L.
In a capacitor the current leads the voltage by 90 degrees. Its opposition is XC equal to 1 over 2 pi f C.
Now plot opposition against frequency. XL rises in a straight line, XC falls along a curve, and R stays flat.
Example: a 0.1 henry coil at 50 hertz. XL is 2 pi times 50 times 0.1, which is 31.4 ohms. Note that a pure L or C uses no power.

text.en: Power in L or C: zero

body.en: An inductor opposes AC by its inductive reactance $X_L = 2πfL$ (ohms). The current lags the voltage by 90°. $X_L$ rises with frequency, and is zero for DC, so a coil passes DC but chokes high-frequency AC. The average power in a *pure inductor* is zero.
body.kn: ಪ್ರೇರಕವು XL = 2πfL ಪ್ರೇರಕ ಪ್ರತಿಘಾತದಿಂದ AC ಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರವಾಹ ವಿಭವಾಂತರಕ್ಕಿಂತ 90° ಹಿಂದುಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಆವೃತ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದಂತೆ XL ಹೆಚ್ಚು; DC ಗೆ ಶೂನ್ಯ. ಸರಾಸರಿ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ಶೂನ್ಯ.

body.en: A *capacitor* opposes AC by its capacitive reactance $X_C = 1/(2πfC)$. The current leads the voltage by 90°. $X_C$ falls as frequency rises and is infinite for DC, so a capacitor blocks DC but passes AC. The average power is zero.

problem.en: A 0.1 H inductor is connected to 230 V, 50 Hz. Find X_L and the current.

steps.en: The current lags the voltage by 90°.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 0.1 H inductor is connected to 230 V, 50 Hz. Find X_L and the current.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 0.1 H inductor is connected to 230 volts, 50 hertz. Find X L and the current.
X L equals 2 pi fL equals 2 times 3.1416 times 50 times 0.1 equals 31.42 ohms.
I equals V over X L equals 230 over 31.42 equals 7.32 A.
The current lags the voltage by 90 degrees.
So the answer is 31.4 ohms; 7.32 A.

problem.en: A 10 µF capacitor is connected to 230 V, 50 Hz. Find X_C and the current.

steps.en: The current leads the voltage by 90°.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 10 µF capacitor is connected to 230 V, 50 Hz. Find X_C and the current.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 10 microfarads capacitor is connected to 230 volts, 50 hertz. Find X C and the current.
X C equals 1 over (2 pi times 50 times 10 times 10 to the power minus 6) equals 1 over (3.1416 times 10 to the power minus 3) equals 318.3 ohms.
I equals 230 over 318.3 equals 0.723 A.
The current leads the voltage by 90 degrees.
So the answer is 318 ohms; 0.72 A.
